facts: A new model-based bundle adjustment algorithm is presented to recover the 3D model of a scene/object from a sequence of images with unknown motions.
A sequence of images has unknown motions in the described setting.
The new model-based bundle adjustment algorithm uses a surface controlled by a small set of parameters.
The new model-based bundle adjustment algorithm does not represent a scene/object by a collection of isolated 3D features (usually points).
The approach has advantages compared with previous model-based approaches.
The approach directly uses the model space as the search space instead of as a regularizer.
Using the model space as the search space results in a more elegant formulation with fewer unknowns and fewer equations.
The new model-based bundle adjustment algorithm automatically associates tracked points with their correct locations on the surfaces.
The new model-based bundle adjustment algorithm eliminates the need for a prior 2D-to-3D association.
For face modeling, the new model-based bundle adjustment algorithm uses a very small set of face metrics (meaningful deformations) to parameterize the face geometry.
Using a very small set of face metrics results in a smaller search space in face modeling.
Using a very small set of face metrics results in a better posed system in face modeling.
Experiments with both synthetic and real data show that the new algorithm is faster than existing ones.
Experiments with both synthetic and real data show that the new algorithm is more accurate than existing ones.
Experiments with both synthetic and real data show that the new algorithm is more stable than existing ones.
